newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln Natl confirms possible unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln Natl confirms possible unit sale.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp confirmed Wednesday it is considering selling its 83.3 percent-owned American States Financial Corp property-casualty business.
"Lincoln National supports the efforts of American States Financial to explore its strategic options," Lincoln National Chairman Ian Rolland said in a statement.

"Lincoln National is evolving from a multi-line insurer into a focused financial services company. For the last five years, Lincoln National has been sharpening its focus on its core wealth accumulation and wealth protection businesses to enhance shareholder value," Rolland said.
"Any proceeds from a sale of American States would be used by Lincoln National to accelerate the profitable growth of our core businesses," he said.
Lincoln National owns and operates financial services businesses that provide annuities, life insurance, life-health reinsurance and property-casualty insurance.

In a statement released from its Indianapolis headquarters, American States said it had hired Goldman Sachs & Co to assist it in exploring strategic options, including the possible sale of the company.

"Consolidation trends in the property-casualty industry may make this an opportune time to fully realize the value of the company," said Robert Anker, American States chairman and chief executive officer.
"We do not intend to make any further statement until the process is complete," he said.

American States is a holding company that, through its subsidiaries, writes business and personal insurance, principally in 43 states, through a nationwide network of 4,800 independent insurance agents.
